name: Wastewater Equalisation Tank
processFunction: Equalise the A-160 residual, A-300 phase 2 / A-400 wash liquors and the A-1100 bleed ahead of neutralisation

design.materialOfConstruction: Dual-laminate FRP/HDPE/rubber-lined CS on raw-acid stages; 316L or coated CS only after pH is reliably ≥6.5
design.feedBasis: Route 2 + 6 residual: 615 m³/d design (25.6 m³/h), ≈ 495 m³/d normal; 24.3 t/d H₂SO₄ design (18.6 firm + 5.8 organics-bleed allowance), HCl 3 t/d (M3) to 18.2 t/d (PFD dose, bounding)

reviewFindings: R-1002 draft targets conflict: 7-10.5 in stage text versus 8.5-10.5 by the reactor. R-1001 draft pH 3-4 is indicative only. BaCl2 polishing is conditional; the draft <1500 mg/L sulfate note is not a verified site discharge limit. HCl trim needs a metals-redissolution review. No dose or control target is approved.

Model 100 m3/h, 15/30/20/20 min residence times, tank inventories and equalization assumptions are layout screening inputs, not measured flows or approved capacities. The model notes 62.208 m3/h eight-module A-400 capacity against a 71 m3/h duty. Upstream batch peaks, returns and actual chemistry remain unreconciled.

The draft permits conditional centrifuge bypass with downtime wording; the model keeps it closed and positively blinded. Downtime alone is not acceptance for A-2000. Centrate recycle improves solids capture only and does not remove dissolved salts. Residual Ba/Ca/sulfate, turbidity, pH and other RO acceptance criteria remain unqualified.

Selected wet vents are candidate connections to HD-3100 only; chemical-storage vents remain separate by service. A-3000 condensate and blowdown returns are normally isolated. Low process drains are positively blinded; no common chemical drain or dry A-800 waste route is inferred. Sludge classification and receiving disposal acceptance require testing, not the draft non-hazardous wording.

Sheet is Draft - Not for Use with XXX revision. Cooling is a separate utility; duties and limits are unqualified. pH, temperature, level and mixing checks are functional concepts only. Legacy spare return connections remain capped; the modeled normal A-2000 backwash return is distinct. Aeration/oxidation remains future provision and is not invented as installed equipment.

identity.acidRoute: Spent-acid recovery, REP-039 Route 2 + 6: TLGO separated from 50–60 wt % acid in A-300 (Route 2) and the GIC from the A-160 acid before washing (Route 6); the filtrates are reconcentrated and recycled, so A-1000 treats only the residual (≈ 6–15 t/d acid). Gated on M1 (filterability at 50–60 wt %), M2 (recycled-acid quality) and M3 (Mn(VII) = 0 before heating); Route 0 (neutralise everything in A-1000) is the fallback
